topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russia warned Ukraine of a 'dangerous trend' after Ukrainian attacks on Russian naval and merchant shipping, with Libya and the Baltic named (4 sources). Russia's Foreign Ministry separately accused Estonia of actions 'on the verge of triggering open war' after Estonia announced closure of their land border (3 sources). Single-source reports say the drone-hit cargo ship Sparta II was towed out of Finnish waters and that storms and drones disrupted Russian Baltic and Black Sea oil loadings. Two outlets say Jared Kushner indicated the US may consider NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine, and Poland says Russia twice tried to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza, and displaced Palestinians are protesting; a Gaza mayor says the destruction of residential buildings is part of a 'gradual displacement' policy (5 sources). Gadi Eisenkot, described as Israel's leading contender for prime minister, says Iran poses no immediate threat before a new government forms. Netanyahu pushed back, and he is accused of pushing for new strikes on Iran to keep power while Trump weighs renewed strikes (3 sources each). Reportedly, an Iranian lawmaker warned that US bases in Britain, Germany and Bulgaria could be targets, and Iran is seeking about US$290 billion in damages from the US. Former Mossad chief David Barnea described Israel's role in foiling a Vienna concert plot.
topics.T15: Stories are disparate and no single event dominates. The most widely carried item (2 sources) concerns flood risk to Franz Josef village in New Zealand. Single-source items cover a fire in Majorca, record St. Johns River flooding in Florida, a 5.3 magnitude earthquake in Nepal, and warnings of an intensifying El Niño. Others are preparedness pieces from Europe, the Philippines and India.
topics.T01: Drone strikes in and around Khartoum reportedly killed at least four people, including a child, and damaged a UN building with staff inside. Amnesty urged a war crimes probe into Ethiopian shelling of Alamata in Tigray (3 sources). Reportedly, six travellers were killed when shelling hit civilian vehicles on a Yemeni highway, and South Korea briefly issued an air-raid warning after Russian jets flew near its airspace.
topics.T02: Coverage is sparse and mixed. Single-source items report a second group of critically ill Gaza children arriving for NHS treatment, Sudanese war widows struggling to support their children, and criticism of the US halt to HIV relief funding. A retrospective on Audrey Hepburn's 1992 Somalia visit is also included.
topics.T04: Two people died in a Legionnaires' disease outbreak in Rotherham, UK (2 sources). Malawi reportedly imposed border checks and quarantine measures to keep out Ebola. Nigeria's Bayelsa community reported an unidentified skin illness suspected to be chickenpox or monkeypox (2 sources). Animal-disease items include a rabbit hemorrhagic disease outbreak in Alberta hares, lumpy skin disease quarantine in Krasnoyarsk Krai, and chronic wasting disease in a Kentucky deer.
topics.T05: Stories are sparse and unconnected. The UK formally recognised the genocide against the Rohingya and announced measures against the Myanmar military. Belgium's PM reportedly warned his government could collapse over a budget impasse, and a Pakistani minister's rare visit to India has prompted speculation about a thaw.
topics.T06: Two people, a mother and son, were jailed for their part in the Ballymena riots of last summer (5 sources). In Brussels, around 50,000 marched against austerity, and clashes at Brussels-South station led to eight arrests, a burning car, and the use of water cannon and tear gas. Opinion pieces warn of possible unrest in Britain, and India's Congress Party reportedly threatened nationwide protests against Meta over alleged account restrictions.
topics.T07: German reports, carried by two outlets, say Russia plans to launch a nuclear warhead into space; the story is based on leaked intelligence and is unverified here. A satellite-imagery analysis by IISS reportedly suggests Russia's RS-28 Sarmat may have entered service, though no outlets are counted for it. Kim Jong Un received the credentials of India's new ambassador (2 sources). A single opinion-style piece claims a US-China-Russia leaders' declaration against nuclear war, which is uncorroborated in this input.
topics.T08: Reported threats and plots include a threat email to Hyderabad police about a 26/11-style attack, the arrest of a Mumbai dockyard trainee for allegedly filming sensitive sites for suspected Pakistani operatives, and a reported US warning about terror risks in Europe over the holidays. Reported attacks include gunmen attacking a Christian archbishop in Syria and a village head and his family killed in Niger State. A GAO investigation reportedly got four AI chatbots to produce terrorist attack plans. The Vienna plot item is covered under Iran / Israel / Middle East.
topics.T10: Japan is drawing auto suppliers into a major arms buildup (4 sources). Pentagon chief Hegseth criticised Canada over NATO spending and F-35 plans (2 sources), and NATO's Rutte urged Britain to set out a credible path to its defence spending pledges. UN talks on binding rules for autonomous weapons will continue through 2028 after the US, Russia and Israel opposed them, and thousands marched in Brussels against military spending.
topics.T11: India and Malaysia held Exercise Harimau Shakti 2026, focused on drone warfare (4 sources). An Indian Army contingent arrived in Nepal for Exercise Surya Kiran, running November 25 to December 8. Reportedly, Polish special forces evaded US troops in NATO's Deep Strike exercise, and two soldiers died when a tank ran over them in a drill in Haryana.
topics.T12: The European Commission confirmed a personal data leak after a cyberattack and warned of further disruption (2 sources). CISA flagged a critical Cisco Expressway flaw as actively exploited. Spanish police reportedly arrested the alleged leader of NoName057(16)'s first physical cell in Spain. Single-source items cite breaches at the USDA and the FBI's crime database, a reported firing of the US National Cyber Director, and an insurer's data showing more than double the cyber incidents in late October than in late May.
topics.T13: Coverage is thin. Malaysia reportedly sought Turkey's help to resettle 10,000 Rohingya after the ICJ genocide ruling against Myanmar. A separate opinion-style piece covers asylum-seeker housing in English villages.
topics.T16: House Democrats clinched at least 258 seats, the largest majority since 1992 (4 sources). Spain holds a snap general election on November 29, with the conservative People's Party and far-right Vox projected to win a combined majority (2 sources). Other items include Swedish Centre Party districts opening to talks on a right-wing government, the DNC's plan for 12 presidential primary debates before 2028, and Indonesia's rescheduling of its vice presidential election to December 11.
